title: EEG-Based Classification of Hypnotic Susceptibility Using Two-Dimensional Convolutional Neural Networks
abstract: arXiv:2610.27738v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Guided Imagery (GI) is a mind-based relaxation technique widely used in clinical and therapeutic settings. Objectively assessing whether a patient has entered a relaxed state remains a challenge for clinicians. This study investigates electroencephalography (EEG)-based classification of hypnotic susceptibility using two-dimensional Convolutional Neural Networks (2D CNNs) applied to minimally preprocessed signals, without manual feature extraction. Data were collected from 62 male participants (32 Control, 30 Hypno) using a 256-channel dense array amplifier during Guided Imagery or cognitive task conditions. A sliding-window framework evaluated up to 868 independent models across seven anatomically defined brain regions and 124 ten-second time windows. translated_title: 基于二维卷积神经网络的脑电图催眠易感性分类
translated_abstract: 引导意象是一种广泛应用于临床和治疗场景的思维放松技术。客观评估患者是否已进入放松状态对临床医生而言仍是一项挑战。本研究探讨了基于脑电图（EEG）的催眠易感性分类，采用二维卷积神经网络（2D CNN）对仅经过最小预处理的信号进行分析，无需人工特征提取。数据采集自62名男性受试者（32名对照组，30名催眠组），使用256通道高密度阵列放大器在引导意象或认知任务条件下记录。研究采用滑动窗口框架，在七个解剖学定义的脑区和124个十秒时间窗口上评估了多达868个独立模型。先通过片段级随机划分进行筛选，随后采用留一被试交叉验证以获得与被试无关的性能估计，并通过集成方法结合预……（摘要在此处截断）
tldr: 本研究利用二维卷积神经网络直接分析最小预处理的脑电信号，结合滑动窗口框架与留一被试交叉验证，实现了无需人工特征提取且与被试无关的催眠易感性客观分类。
en_tdlr: This study classifies hypnotic susceptibility from minimally preprocessed EEG signals using 2D CNNs, employing a sliding-window framework with Leave-One-Subject-Out cross-validation to achieve subject-independent classification without manual feature extraction.
